claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The narrative describes the fact that Robert fell asleep while driving, which is circumstantial evidence of negligence rather than an out-of-court statement.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) defines hearsay as an out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted; circumstantial evidence does not qualify.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that Robert fell asleep while driving

arguments.text: There is no indication in the narrative of any oral or written declaration made by Robert or another person out of court.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires an 'out-of-court statement' (oral, written, or nonverbal assertion) to trigger hearsay analysis.

arguments.text: The fact of falling asleep is offered to prove negligence directly through conduct, not through an assertion.
arguments.legal_rule: Conduct offered to prove a fact it tends to prove is not hearsay unless it is intended as an assertion.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether Robert negligently drove, the fact that Robert fell asleep while driving.
